### CSRF tokens for listener ack mutations
- id: `rm-115` | track: security | priority: 30.0 | status: completed (implemented 2026-09-24 as B4 of docs/prioritization/2026-09-24-cycle-1-batch.md, run 6cbc2a1d implement attempt a292009c; landed 2026-09-26 at this integrate of run 6cbc2a1d into main's 0ca643e lineage — conflict case f3c5735b; B4 rides unchanged from the batch's implement tree, no re-implementation needed)
- signals: `src/routes/listener.ts:121,130` accept session-authenticated state-changing POSTs (`/messages/:id/ack`, `/ack-all`) protected only by SameSite=Lax cookies, while logout already implements an explicit CSRF-token dance (`src/routes/auth.ts:168-190`) — an asymmetry; exploit window is narrow (Lax blocks cross-site POSTs except the fresh-cookie grace period) and impact bounded (ack state)

- implementation (2026-09-24; landed at the 2026-09-26 integrate of run 6cbc2a1d): `deriveAckCsrfToken` (HMAC-SHA256 over the cookie key + operator login, 1h validity window with current+previous acceptance) mirrors the logout dance; `GET /api/listener/csrf` mints the token; both mutations verify via `x-csrf-token` with `timingSafeEqual` and fail closed 403 on missing/invalid token or unavailable CSRF material (503 when standalone-config lacks the cookie key); web client fetches the token per mutation and never posts without one; contract updated in `docs/contracts/operator-listener-channel.md`; 5 new server route tests (incl. wrong-operator 403 and standalone-null-config paths) + 5 ack-flow web client tests (3 updated, 2 net-new fail-closed), all in the 3127-test green run

### Cookie-key canonical-format enforcement
- id: `rm-206` | track: security | priority: 55.0 | status: implemented 2026-09-25 (landed at the c2ae28ab integrate — authored in-batch as rm-165, renumbered because landed meanings own ids; conflict case 6a7122e8)
- signals: `loadCookieKey`/`decodeKey` previously accepted lenient decodings — stripped-padding base64, non-canonical hex/base64 lengths, and raw UTF-8 passphrases all silently loaded via Node's lenient decoders, so a misprovisioned cookie key booted and signed instead of failing at startup; a 44-char all-hex input fell through to a base64 mis-decode (the "44 A's" exploit path yielding 33 null bytes)
- acceptance: the encoded key form must be the exact canonical encoding of its decoded bytes — hex at 2 chars/byte or padded base64 at 4 chars per 3 bytes, decoding to ≥32 bytes; non-canonical encodings, degenerate (single-repeated-byte) keys, and raw passphrases throw fail-fast with specific messages at load; documented in README.md's Configuration section

- id: `rm-557` | track: security | priority: 24.0 | status: implemented (2026-10-04, cycle-3 batch B, run b528f707 implement 1599ea1e, compound 715e078f; minted by the same run's roadmap a941c4af from research 8f95126f C3, verified unowned at mint; implemented at base 227375247 — pending review/ship)

  - no feature the app actually uses is denied (grep web/src for each denied feature name stays zero-hit)

- id: `rm-656` | track: reliability | priority: 14.0 | status: implemented 2026-10-05 (added 2026-10-05, run 5e66155863354a2d8eb63fe6beeaabd8 assess 77b8759 + research ecae3ba9 R1 — repository-maintenance cycle:1; verified unowned by content: ROADMAP item-text greps for verifyDepsBeforeRun / auto-install / auto-rewrite / silent rewrite = 0 hits; hazard first observed 2026-10-05 run ae40aa7a (a fresh clone's first pnpm command dirties a tracked file; two audit/gate evidence-contamination incidents that morning); control A/B-proven by research ecae3ba9; minted rm-656 above the all-lineage ceiling rm-655 — sibling run-e795cadd's uncommitted candidate def timestamped 2026-10-05T04:18Z — with in-file max rm-613)
- signals: pnpm 11.28.3 (the packageManager pin) auto-installs when `pnpm <script>` runs against a stale tree; at the current broken tree (pnpm-lock.yaml:8-12 overrides vs pnpm-workspace.yaml:43-46 floors — the 1e1e2f5 wall) ANY script run rewrites pnpm-lock.yaml in place: control arm /tmp/vdb-ecae run2 (2026-10-05) ced1e543 -> 9abdcdd5, "Done in 12.3s"; the misleading diagnostic is `pnpm config get verify-deps-before-run` returning undefined (the honored key is the camelCase pnpm-workspace.yaml form)

### snapshot-store byte bound counts UTF-16 code units
- id: `rm-701` | track: reliability | priority: 34.0 | status: implemented 2026-10-07 (run 5b333105a22a47cfb4daedf2b68bc8b0 implement 953ec00ebc904dd98bb08b0d8f8ddf68, pre-review in the cycle-1 batch at base 25d32be; added 2026-10-07, repository-maintenance cycle:1 run 5b333105a22a47cfb4daedf2b68bc8b0 roadmap e743deac21a14a8ba3d4479624937bc6, from assess fd1ac83b F2 — fresh and untracked at 25d32be; minted above the all-lineage dashboard ceiling rm-699, id-basis recorded on the batch's rm-700 (deduped into rm-744 at the 2026-10-08 integrate, conflict case 76d683f2); same defect class as rm-114's SSE-reader cap — tracked as a sibling surface because the snapshot path is the aggregation pipeline, not the operator stream)
- signals: src/github/snapshot-store.ts:29 caps at MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES = 1_048_576 (BYTES-named) but :96 (raw) and :122 (serialized) compare String.length — UTF-16 code units, not bytes; a CJK/astral-heavy snapshot therefore trips the cap at up to ~2x the nominal byte bound (or ~2x early under the strict reading), the same class rm-114 pins for the operator SSE pair and src/listener/contract.ts already cures with Buffer.byteLength
- acceptance: both cap comparisons measure bytes (Buffer.byteLength or an equivalent single-site helper); a round-trip property test with astral-plane and CJK payloads pins the bound at exactly 1_048_576 bytes; the constant's name and its comment agree with the measured unit
- evidence: targeted vitest on snapshot-store round-trips red-before/green-after; the byte-count assertion values cited in the cycle batch doc
- implementation (2026-10-07, run 5b333105a22a47cfb4daedf2b68bc8b0 implement 953ec00ebc904dd98bb08b0d8f8ddf68, cycle-1 batch): both cap sites (src/github/snapshot-store.ts:106 load, :132 persist) now measure utf8ByteLength — a single Buffer.byteLength('utf8') helper whose doc comment names the unit, mirroring the listener contract's helper; MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES = 1_048_576 and its 1-MiB comment unchanged and now truthful; both warning sites log bytes, not length. Tests pin the inclusive boundary both directions (exactly-at-cap loads; +1 byte rejected), the defect directly (a CJK snapshot over the byte cap but UNDER the code-unit cap is rejected on load AND not persisted — String.length admitted both pre-fix), and a fast-check property (40 runs) over astral+CJK code-point names with targets CAP±4 asserting loads iff at-or-under the byte cap plus round-trip under it. Red-first: the CJK, property, and boundary tests fail against the pre-fix source.
- pre-review validation (2026-10-08, same envelope as rm-700's rider — targeted_tests 7a2daf76 + full_tests ebc5e988, consumed as recorded evidence at compound): test/snapshot-store.test.ts ran green inside the 747-test targeted set (inclusive boundary both directions, the over-byte-cap-under-code-unit-cap CJK defect case on load AND persist, fast-check 40-run astral/CJK property); full CI 11/11 at ephemeral PR #433 exercises the utf8ByteLength helper on the live aggregation path

- id: `rm-702` | track: reliability | priority: 30.0 | status: implemented 2026-10-07 (run 5b333105a22a47cfb4daedf2b68bc8b0 implement 953ec00ebc904dd98bb08b0d8f8ddf68, pre-review in the cycle-1 batch at base 25d32be; added 2026-10-07, repository-maintenance cycle:1 run 5b333105a22a47cfb4daedf2b68bc8b0 roadmap e743deac21a14a8ba3d4479624937bc6, from assess fd1ac83b F3 — fresh and untracked at 25d32be; minted above the all-lineage dashboard ceiling rm-699, id-basis recorded on the batch's rm-700 (deduped into rm-744 at the 2026-10-08 integrate, conflict case 76d683f2))
- signals: src/server.ts:1627 gates the listener on import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}` — a literal template string, not a file-URL comparison; under a path containing characters that URL-encode (a space, or any char outside the unreserved set) the two sides differ (import.meta.url percent-encodes, `argv[1]` does not) and the server boots WITHOUT starting its listener; empirically probed 2026-10-07: node x.mjs launched from '/tmp/dir with space' → the check evaluates FALSE
- acceptance: the entry-point test compares via `url.pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href === import.meta.url` (or an equivalent pathToFileURL normalization); a regression test pins entry-detection TRUE under a space-containing path; no behavior change for plain paths
- evidence: targeted vitest or a node -e probe matrix (plain path, space path) recorded in the cycle batch doc; the fix diff cited on this item's implementation record when it lands
- implementation (2026-10-07, run 5b333105a22a47cfb4daedf2b68bc8b0 implement 953ec00ebc904dd98bb08b0d8f8ddf68, cycle-1 batch): the autostart gate (src/server.ts:1648) now calls exported `isMainEntryPoint(import.meta.url, process.argv[1])` — a pure comparator on `url.pathToFileURL(argv1).href` with explicit undefined/empty-argv and unencodable-argv guards (never autostart); plain-path behavior unchanged. test/server-entry-point.test.ts pins the pure comparison (plain path, the space defect case, parentheses/non-ASCII/a+b%z paths, mismatched argv, absent/empty argv) AND re-runs the assess probe for real: a spawned Node entry file inside a mkdtemp 'dir with space ' directory reports ENTRY-TRUE where the pre-fix template evaluated FALSE. - pre-review validation (2026-10-08, targeted_tests 7a2daf76 + full_tests ebc5e988, consumed as recorded evidence at compound): the impacted-suite runner derives only TRACKED test files, so the NEW untracked test/server-entry-point.test.ts ran as an explicit supplementary leg — 1 file / 6 tests ALL PASS rc=0 (the tracked-only enumeration class is recorded in the 2026-10-08 lessons doc); full CI 11/11 at ephemeral PR #433 boots the entry surface end-to-end

Implemented as an injectable SnapshotStore seam with a JSON-file-backed store — src/github/snapshot-store.ts (DASHBOARD_SNAPSHOT_CACHE, fail-open on any load/persist fault, 2 MiB size cap, atomic tmp+rename writes) rather than the acceptance's node:sqlite sketch; restart-only semantics preserved (no intra-cycle TTL, superseding the rm-112 rationale) and the seam is injectable so a node:sqlite-backed store swaps in without touching the aggregator; the boot seed is served forced-stale under rm-197's banner contract, and ALL 7 snapshot writes route through one setSnapshot site (single persist chokepoint). The aaa84dff-credited fail-closed rehydrate-after-metadata-read answer is implemented as scrubLastGoodAgainstDenylist: a fresh metadata read re-scrubs the boot-seeded/carried last-good snapshot BEFORE any serve path, so a repo redacted between persist and restart is never re-served (the 2026-06-25 redaction concern, closed downstream of the same metadata gate the live cycle obeys); 13 new tests (9 aggregator bridge + 4 store). Originally: candidate, added 2026-09-25, cycle-14 batch, run ec07634c; decision-gated — supersedes the rm-112 TTL-removal rationale restart-only, never intra-cycle; gated on rm-197 landing first; PARALLEL RE-PROPOSE credited 2026-09-25 at the aaa84dff integrate: the cycle-13 batch's rm-188 (dedupe, item released) reached the same node:sqlite restart-bridge frame independently and adds the fail-closed answer to the 2026-06-25 redaction concern — rehydrate only after a successful metadata/repos.yaml read with the denylist reapplied before serving, i.e. downstream of the same metadata gate the live cycle obeys)

- acceptance: persist the last good snapshot (node:sqlite mirroring the listener-store pattern) and serve it at boot bannered-stale until the first refresh completes; decision frame: restart-only semantics with no intra-cycle TTL, no API-budget motive, explicit supersession of the rm-112 rationale recorded in the implementing batch doc
- evidence: gated on rm-197's in-flight contract landing first; a future cycle decides the bridge against the decision frame recorded in docs/prioritization/2026-09-25-cycle-14-batch.md §Parked

### Operator stream stall watchdog and a Last-Event-ID resume decision
- id: `rm-220` | track: reliability | priority: 50.0 | status: candidate (added 2026-09-24, run 449ed1a5 assess F5 + research; complements rm-114's parser work; RENUMBERED rm-164→rm-220 at the 2026-09-25 integrate of run 449ed1a5, conflict case e7b03a2f — main's rm-164 is the landed prose-residue guard)
